research_question: Among patients with pain conditions, what is the effect of a single sympathetic nerve block, compared with standard care, on pain score at 14 days after the block, excluding pain outcomes measured at other timepoints from this analysis?
control_label: Standard care without sympathetic nerve block
outcome_description: Pain intensity or pain severity score measured at 14 days after a single sympathetic nerve block. Pool the 14-day pain outcome only; do not substitute or combine outcomes from other follow-up times such as 1 month. When a study reports multiple eligible pain instruments at day 14, prespecify a hierarchy favoring the study's primary pain measure, then a validated multi-item pain scale, then a unidimensional numeric rating scale or visual analogue scale, to avoid double-counting participants.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means that a single sympathetic nerve block produces lower (better) pain scores at 14 days than standard care.
search_queries: sympathetic nerve block pain controlled trial
single sympathetic block pain standard care comparison
sympathetic blockade pain score 14 days quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies in patients with a pain condition that evaluate a single sympathetic nerve block and include a standard-care comparison condition.
Studies reporting pain intensity or severity at 14 days after treatment, or providing data clearly attributable to the 14-day assessment.
Studies reporting sufficient quantitative information, directly or through obtainable supplementary or author-provided data, to calculate an effect size for the treatment-versus-control comparison.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded.
No comparison between a single sympathetic nerve block treatment condition and a standard-care control condition.
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size; means and standard deviations, t/F-values, proportions, or odds ratios are required.
Completely unrelated to sympathetic nerve block treatment, pain, or the specified 14-day outcome.
moderators_to_extract: anatomical type and level of sympathetic block
local anesthetic or injectate and dose
effect_size_note: For continuous pain scores, calculate a small-sample-corrected standardized mean difference and orient signs so positive values favor the nerve block (less pain). Prefer change-from-baseline effects when both groups report compatible change scores; otherwise use 14-day endpoint scores. Account for clustering, crossover designs, and shared control groups where applicable. Use only the 14-day assessment in this analysis and do not substitute nearest later or earlier timepoints without a prespecified sensitivity rule.
